_about: Two tunable lists of strings we recognise. Both are deliberately data
rather than code, for the same reason as data/functional-properties.json:
they will be tuned for the life of the project, and an operator with an
unusual site needs to override them without waiting for a release.
Neither will ever be complete. That is fine — this is the cheap majority
of what would otherwise need a language model, and the cost of a missing
entry is one unreported finding rather than a false one.
_placeholders: Values a generator or theme emits when a setting was never configured.
Each entry records where it was actually seen, so a future reader can tell
an evidenced pattern from a guessed one.
Matching is case-insensitive and against the TRIMMED whole value. Anchor
every pattern: 'Lorem Ipsum Generator' is a legitimate product name, and a
site that sells one would otherwise be told its product is a placeholder.
The one deliberate exception is 'unexecuted template code', which cannot
anchor because template code is a fragment by nature — it turns up wrapped
in whatever text surrounded it. It is safe unanchored because no legitimate
value contains '<?php'. Do not add a second exception without the same

placeholders.label: WordPress/Yoast default site name
placeholders.note: One corpus site publishes this as both the Organization name and the logo caption on all 150 pages. The site is telling consumers it is called 'My Website'.

placeholders.label: WordPress default tagline
placeholders.note: The stock tagline. Not seen in this corpus but universally recognised.

placeholders.label: lorem ipsum
placeholders.note: Whole-value only. power-plugins.com legitimately sells a lorem ipsum generator, and substring matching would flag it.

placeholders.label: unexecuted template code
placeholders.note: One corpus site publishes '<?php the_author(); ?>' as the author name on all 150 pages — the theme emits the PHP literally instead of running it. Deliberately the one substring rule in this file: template code is a fragment by nature and never anchors, and no legitimate value contains '<?php'. Also covers Yoast's %%title%% replacement variables and Mustache/Twig braces.

_benign_media_hosts: Hosts that legitimately serve media for somebody else's site, so an image
pointing at one is not a finding.
A subdomain of the site's own registrable domain is always benign and is
handled in code rather than listed here — cdn.example.com serving
example.com's images is the normal shape of a CDN, and headwall-hosting.com
Gravatar dominates: it appears on 7 of 22 corpus sites as the author avatar
of every WordPress user. Without it here, this check would fire on most
_media_properties: Properties whose value is a media resource. A foreign host on one of these
is a finding; a foreign host on `sameAs` is the entire point of `sameAs`.
